name: API Governance Ruleset Registry
description: A curated, machine-readable registry of adoptable, provenanced API-governance rulesets — national, industry, security, company, and community rulesets you can adopt by reference instead of running the linter's defaults. Maintained by API Commons. PRs welcome.

categories.national: Owned and maintained by a national or sub-national government as public policy.
categories.industry: Encodes a cross-vendor industry standard or specification (e.g. JSON:API, a sector API standard).
categories.security: Focused on API security posture — OWASP API Security Top 10 and related hardening rules.
categories.company: A single company's public API standards, published as an adoptable ruleset.
categories.community: Maintained by an individual or open community as a shared, reusable ruleset.
categories.vendor-default: The linter or tool's own built-in default. Config, not a standard — carries no naming, ownership, or domain rules.

rulesets.name: Italian API OAS Checker
rulesets.description: The Italian government's official Spectral ruleset enforcing the Modello di Interoperabilità (ModI) and the national API design guidelines against OpenAPI definitions. The reference example of a governed national ruleset adopted by reference.

provenance.owner: Dipartimento per la trasformazione digitale, Presidency of the Council of Ministers (Italy)

adoptVia.note: Reference the hosted ruleset directly from your .spectral.yml `extends`. A pinned release is also published at https://github.com/italia/api-oas-checker-rules/releases.

rulesets.notes: The exemplar for this registry: pulled remotely in the wild by teamdigitale/* and italia/* pipelines (e.g. teamdigitale/dati-semantic-backend, italia/spid-cie-oidc-schemas) rather than copied. A real owned, versioned, government-maintained standard.

rulesets.name: NL API Design Rules (ADR)
rulesets.publisher: Dutch Government — developer.overheid.nl / NL API Strategie
rulesets.description: The machine-readable Spectral encoding of the Netherlands' API Design Rules (ADR), the national standard for government REST APIs, hosted for direct remote adoption.

provenance.owner: Logius / NL API Strategie working group (Kennisplatform APIs), Dutch central government

adoptVia.note: Version-pin against a specific ADR release (e.g. /adr/2.1/); the unversioned /adr/ruleset.yaml tracks latest.

rulesets.notes: A national government standard published specifically to be consumed remotely. Seen extended by Dutch public-sector pipelines (BRP-API, lvbag, VNG-Realisatie) in the research corpus.

rulesets.name: Haal Centraal Common (VNG)
rulesets.description: Shared Spectral rules governing the Dutch municipal Haal Centraal API family, extended across the VNG-Realisatie and BRP-API repositories so every municipal-data API is linted against one common standard.

provenance.owner: VNG Realisatie, on behalf of Dutch municipalities

adoptVia.note: Extended remotely by the individual Haal-Centraal API repos rather than duplicated in each.

rulesets.notes: A sub-national / sector-of-government shared ruleset — a real-world hub-and-spoke example where many API repos consume one owned rule source.

rulesets.name: Spectral OWASP API Security
rulesets.description: A Spectral ruleset that encodes the OWASP API Security Top 10 as automated checks against OpenAPI definitions — auth, rate limiting, mass-assignment, error handling, and more.

provenance.owner: Stoplight / open-source maintainers (Andrew Farries, Roberto Polli et al.)

adoptVia.note: Install and `extends` it, or reference the built ruleset at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stoplightio/spectral-owasp-ruleset/main/dist/ruleset.yaml

rulesets.notes: The de-facto community security ruleset; a governed, versioned standard rather than a linter default.

rulesets.name: API Commons OWASP Ruleset
rulesets.description: The API Commons sibling security ruleset — a curated, governed OWASP API Security Top 10 Spectral ruleset published in the @api-common family alongside this registry.

adoptVia.note: Part of the API Commons tool family; being developed alongside ruleset-commons.

rulesets.notes: In development. Listed here so the supply side of the API Commons stack is self-referential and discoverable.

rulesets.name: Spectral built-in OAS ruleset (spectral:oas)
rulesets.description: Spectral's own bundled ruleset for OpenAPI 2/3 (and spectral:asyncapi for AsyncAPI). Structural and validity checks only.

provenance.owner: Stoplight — this is the linter's default config, not an organizational standard

adoptVia.note: Built into Spectral; no install needed. `spectral:asyncapi` is the AsyncAPI equivalent.

rulesets.notes: Config, not a standard. The research found 63% of 1,005 pipelines run exactly this kind of implicit default — it carries no naming, ownership, or domain rules. Listed here, honestly labeled, so teams see what they are actually running.

rulesets.name: Redocly recommended ruleset
rulesets.description: Redocly CLI's built-in `recommended` (and `minimal`) rule configuration for OpenAPI, applied via redocly.yaml.

provenance.owner: Redocly — a tool default, not an organizational standard

adoptVia.note: Add to redocly.yaml. Redocly is a different linter from Spectral, but the same 'default vs owned standard' distinction applies.

rulesets.notes: Config, not a standard. Included to show the same default trap exists outside Spectral.

rulesets.name: vacuum recommended ruleset
rulesets.description: vacuum's built-in recommended rules — a fast, Spectral-compatible OpenAPI linter's default configuration.

provenance.owner: quobix / vacuum project — a tool default, not an organizational standard

adoptVia.value:
# vacuum lint uses recommended rules by default
vacuum lint openapi.yaml
adoptVia.note: vacuum consumes Spectral-format rulesets, so any governed ruleset in this registry can replace the default.

rulesets.notes: Config, not a standard. vacuum can consume the owned rulesets listed here — swap the default for one.

rulesets.name: Baloise Spectral Ruleset
rulesets.description: Baloise's public Spectral ruleset implementing the Zalando RESTful API Guidelines as enforceable rules for the company's OpenAPI definitions.

adoptVia.note: A company operationalizing an industry standard (Zalando) as a concrete, adoptable ruleset.

rulesets.notes: Good example of the standard-to-ruleset path: an industry guideline turned into a machine-readable, owned company ruleset.

rulesets.name: SailPoint API Linter
rulesets.description: SailPoint's open API linter — a root Spectral ruleset (plus product-specific rulesets) encoding SailPoint's REST API standards.

adoptVia.note: Additional path/schema rulesets live alongside the root ruleset in the same repo.

rulesets.notes: A vendor publishing its own governed API standards as an adoptable ruleset.

rulesets.name: DevOps API Linter
rulesets.description: A shared, general-purpose Spectral ruleset for consistent REST API design (naming, versioning, responses) intended for DevOps CI pipelines.

adoptVia.note: Reference the raw rules.yaml directly from your .spectral.yml `extends`.

rulesets.notes: The single most-referenced remote ruleset in the 1,005-pipeline research corpus — 74 pipelines extend this one URL. Proof that a good shared ruleset gets adopted widely by reference.

rulesets.name: Ignitia Spectral Validators
rulesets.description: Ignitia's shared Spectral ruleset, published so its API repositories lint against one common, remotely-referenced standard.

adoptVia.note: Consumed remotely by Ignitia's API pipelines.

rulesets.notes: Another real remote/shared ruleset observed in the corpus.

rulesets.name: Spectral JSON:API Ruleset
rulesets.description: A Spectral ruleset validating OpenAPI definitions against the JSON:API specification — structure, member names, relationships, and content negotiation.

adoptVia.note: Encodes an industry media-type spec (JSON:API) as adoptable rules.

rulesets.notes: Represents the 'industry standard as ruleset' category — conformance to a cross-vendor spec rather than one org's house style.

rulesets.name: Zalando RESTful API Guidelines
rulesets.description: Zalando's widely-cited RESTful API Guidelines — a de-facto industry reference for REST design that many organizations adopt or fork.

adoptVia.note: The guidelines themselves are prose; the most complete machine-readable Spectral encoding is Baloise's zalando.yml. Zalando also maintains the Zally linter (github.com/zalando/zally).

rulesets.notes: Illustrates the gap between a published standard (prose) and its adoptable machine-readable form (a ruleset). Cross-referenced with the Baloise entry.

rulesets.name: JayTech Spectral Ruleset
rulesets.description: A hosted, remotely-adoptable Spectral ruleset for OpenAPI consistency, published at a stable URL for `extends`.

adoptVia.note: A community example of hosting a ruleset at a dedicated, stable domain for adoption by reference.

rulesets.notes: Observed extended remotely in the research corpus.

rulesets.name: Stoplight Spectral Standard
rulesets.description: Stoplight's opinionated 'standard' ruleset that layers naming and consistency conventions on top of the built-in spectral:oas structural checks.

adoptVia.note: Goes beyond spectral:oas by adding style/consistency rules — closer to an owned standard than a bare default.

rulesets.notes: The bridge between a vendor default and a governed standard: a named, versioned ruleset that adds design conventions.
